title: Geometric stalks of etale sum extension
statement:
Let $u:U\to X$ be an etale morphism of schemes [def-weil-etale-morphism], let $A$ be a commutative ring, and let $F$ be a sheaf of modules over the constant ring $A_U$ on the small etale site of $U$ [def-weil-pbc-etale-site, def-weil-pbc-etale-sheaves]. Let $u_!F$ be the sheafified direct-sum presheaf [def-weil-pbc-etale-sum-extension]. For every geometric point $\bar x:\operatorname{Spec}\Omega\to X$ with $\Omega$ algebraically closed [def-weil-geometric-point], there is a natural $A$-linear isomorphism
$$
(u_!F)_{\bar x}\xrightarrow{\sim}\bigoplus_{\bar z:\operatorname{Spec}\Omega\to U,\ u\bar z=\bar x}F_{\bar z}.
$$
Stalks are geometric stalks [def-weil-pbc-geometric-stalks]. Under this isomorphism the germ represented by a section $s\in F(V\xrightarrow{a}U)$ in the summand indexed by $a$ of the presheaf on a pointed etale neighbourhood $(V,\bar v)$ of $\bar x$ is sent to the germ of $s$ in the summand indexed by $a\bar v$.

proof.text: Put $P(V)=\bigoplus_{a:V\to U\text{ over }X}F(V,a)$, with restrictions as in the definition of sum extension, and put $L=\varinjlim_{(V,\bar v)}P(V)$ in $A$-modules. Fix a small presentation of the small etale site in the universe used for these stalk colimits. Module sheafification has underlying abelian sheaf the abelian sheafification, by the module-sheafification definition. The sheafification unit therefore induces an isomorphism $\theta:L\to(u_!F)_{\bar x}$ by preservation of geometric stalks under abelian sheafification. This map is $A$-linear since the unit and all restriction maps are $A$-linear. An inverse of a bijective $A$-linear map is $A$-linear: apply $\theta$ to the additivity and scalar identities for the proposed inverse.

proof.text: Write $B=\bigoplus_{u\bar z=\bar x}F_{\bar z}$. For every pointed etale neighbourhood $(V,\bar v)$ of $\bar x$ and every $X$-map $a:V\to U$, etale cancellation makes $a$ etale, so $(V,\bar v)$ over $U$ is a pointed neighbourhood of $\bar z=a\bar v$. Send the $a$-summand section $s$ to its germ in the $\bar z$-summand of $B$, and extend by finite sums. If $h:(V\prime,\bar v\prime)\to(V,\bar v)$ is a refinement, then $(ah)\bar v\prime=a\bar v$ and the germs of $s$ and $h^*s$ agree by the stalk colimit relations. These maps are thus a cocone, yielding an $A$-linear map $e:L\to B$.

proof.text: For each lift $\bar z$, construct a map $i_{\bar z}:F_{\bar z}\to L$ as follows. A pointed etale neighbourhood $(W,\bar w)$ of $\bar z$ has structure map $b:W\to U$. Since both $b$ and $u$ are etale, $ub:W\to X$ is etale; view $(W,\bar w)$ as a neighbourhood of $\bar x$. Send $t\in F(W,b)$ to the class in $L$ of $t$ in the $b$-summand of $P(W)$. For every pointed $U$-map $h:W\prime\to W$, restriction in $P$ sends that summand to the $bh$-summand and the colimit relation identifies the two classes. The maps are a cocone for the stalk diagram defining $F_{\bar z}$, so they uniquely induce $i_{\bar z}$. Taking finite sums defines $i:B\to L$.

source.place: Tag 0710, lemma-stalk-j-shriek, final colimit indexed by (phi:V to U,y) with u(phi)(y)=x; explicit inverse to the displayed regrouping

proof.text: For a section $t\in F(W,b)$ at a neighbourhood of $\bar z$, $e i_{\bar z}$ sends its germ to that same germ in the $\bar z$-summand. The colimit universal property gives $e i_{\bar z}$ equal to the summand inclusion for every $\bar z$, hence $ei=\mathrm{id}_B$ by finite sums. Conversely, for $s\in F(V,a)$ in any summand of $P(V)$ at $(V,\bar v)$, $ie$ sends its class first to its germ at $a\bar v$, then back to its original class, using precisely the same neighbourhood $(V,a,\bar v)$ in the definition of $i_{a\bar v}$. Thus $ie$ is the identity on every summand of every coprojection $P(V)\to L$, and hence on $L$ by the colimit universal property. Therefore $e$ and $i$ are inverse $A$-linear isomorphisms.

source.place: Tag 0710, lemma-stalk-j-shriek, the two final displayed equalities, with inverse identities expanded

proof.text: The required isomorphism is $e\theta^{-1}$. A section $s$ in the $a$-summand of $P(V)$ represents $\theta([s])$ in the sheaf stalk, so this isomorphism sends it to its germ in the $a\bar v$-summand, exactly as asserted. For a morphism $\alpha:F\to G$, both composites in the naturality square send each such $s$ to the germ of $\alpha_{(V,a)}(s)$ in the same summand. Equality follows first on finite sums, then from the stalk colimit universal property. Sheafification-unit naturality identifies this square with the one for $(u_!F)_{\bar x}$.
